subject: iterative purification DIF procedure without known anchor items

messages.author: 00be31dadfa803c9
messages.subject: iterative purification DIF procedure without known anchor items
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to use the mirt package for my dissertation to examine DIF of a screening scale across gender and racial groups. I'm having trouble finding a "translated" method from the iterative procedure proposed by Tay et al. (2015) "An overview and practical guide to IRT measurement equivalence analysis", when non-DIF items are identified as anchor items and then used to put the reference and focal groups on the same scale for subsequent DIF analyses. The authors used IRTPRO for their analyses and I would like to use this procedure, but using the mirt package in R. 

These are the steps outlined in Tay et al. (2015):
1. constraining all items to be equal across group(s) and estimating the latent trait distributions (mean and variance) for the focal group(s)
2. focal group(s) trait distributions are fixed at values found in Step 1 and item parameters are freely estimated across groups

Can this procedure be done with the mirt package? 

I have seen other methods that use all other items as anchor items in the first reference model to identify anchor items, is this analogous to the iterative procedure? 

Thank you for any help in advance!
Anna

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: iterative purification DIF procedure without known anchor items
parts:
Hi Anna,

Iterative methods to find suitable anchor items are inherently problematic in that they can be tricked in one way or another, but could be useful at the outside to at least get a feel for suitable equivalent (or rather, lack of evidence against non-equivalence, if one thinks in terms of null hypothesis testing). Regarding the Tay (2015) approach you described, yes mirt's multipleGroup() function can do this.

1) Using the invariance argument, pass the names of the items in the data object, which constrains all the parameters to be equal, and add the flags 'free_means' and 'free_var' to freely estimate the latent mean/variance in the focal group.
2) Given the model in 1, change the starting values of the model using the START argument in the model syntax (see ?mirt.model), and also use the FIXED keyword to fix these to the corresponding starting values. 
3) Loop over the items you suspect to have DIF, or let mirt's DIF() function do that for you by supplying the model defined in 2 (feel free to ignore the warnings about freely estimating the mean/variance terms at this point).

HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: iterative purification DIF procedure without known anchor items
parts:
Hi Phil,

Thank you for your response! I have a follow up now that I have been able to try this iterative approach:
    1. I started with the first step to constrain item parameters and then estimate latent trait distribution of the focal groups, which worked without issue.
         mod1 <- multipleGroup(data, 1, group, invariance = c(colnames(data), 'free_means', 'free_var'))
    2.  Then I attempted to write a mirt.model string using the START and FIXED keywords for all items (1-9) with the focal group [F]
          s <- 'F = 1-9
              START [F] = (GROUP, MEAN_1, 0), (GROUP, COV_11, 1)
              (1-9, a1, 1.0), (1-9, d, 0.0)
              FIXED [F] = (GROUP, MEAN_1), (GROUP, COV_11),
              (1-9, a1), (1-9, d)'
        mod2 <- multipleGroup(data, s, group)

This gave me: Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
  trying to get slot "par" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with no slots
In addition: Warning message:
In FUN(X[[i]], ...) : NAs introduced by coercion

I'm still quite new to mirt() and defining a mirt.model, if you have any insight on how to correctly define the mirt.model, that would be very helpful!

Thanks again,
Anna
